tiers.basis: The claim is a figure about the dataset's scale; if untrue, the team's engineers meet it when they load and inspect the shipped SQLite and JSONL files, which they can do cheaply. Its failure alone changes nothing about the adoption. Rated on the scale alone.

The claim is a figure about the dataset's scale; if untrue, the team's engineers meet it when they load and inspect the shipped files, which they can do cheaply. Its failure alone changes nothing about the adoption. Rated on the scale alone.

If one of the two named files is absent or differently named, the engineers meet this when setting up and can work from the other format; the claim is a packaging detail an operator acts on. Its failure alone changes nothing for the buyer. Rated on the scale alone.

The claim could be untrue because the released database is absent or does not actually contain ground truth, relevance judgments or split labels; without ground truth in the release the team's evaluation results and training rewards would be meaningless and no local repair restores them. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "ground truth or scoring that does not work as described".

The claim could be untrue because one or more of the four named tasks is not actually supported by the released data with usable ground truth over multi-visit timelines. The team would then have to evaluate on fewer tasks and narrow its publication, and it cannot easily author replacement tasks with credible ground truth. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim could be untrue because no training split is released, or the released split does not support training or fine-tuning. Training the agent, including reinforcement learning on the training split, is half the team's stated purpose, and it cannot redraw or repair a missing or unusable split itself without the project's sampling records. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

Any way the claim could be untrue admits real patient data in the release. No patch by the team could cure that, and adoption ends under the buyer's stated walk-away condition. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "data that is not fully synthetic".

The claim could be untrue because the records were not generated as described — for example because they were derived from real patient content rather than produced by the stated synthetic generation — in which case the release is not fully synthetic and adoption ends; other deviations would leave the team publishing provenance claims the materials do not support, which it cannot repair itself. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "data that is not fully synthetic".

The claim is a schema detail the engineers act on when querying the patients table; a wrong table or column list is met on first use and corrected in their own queries. Its failure alone changes nothing for the buyer. Rated on the scale alone.

The claim is a file-structure detail the engineers act on when parsing the JSONL file; a wrong nesting shape is met at setup and corrected in their own reader code. Its failure alone changes nothing for the buyer. Rated on the scale alone.

The claim is a file-format detail; if the file is not SQLite 3 or does not hold the benchmark tables, the engineers meet this the first time they open it and can obtain or inspect the data another way. Its failure alone changes nothing for the buyer. Rated on the scale alone.

If the module is absent or fails to migrate the data, the Docker Compose first-boot Postgres schema creation and benchmark load is another way the project's documents describe for getting the data into the simulator, and a broken command is met and worked around at setup. Its failure alone changes nothing for the buyer. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim is a column-level schema detail the engineers act on when reading the patients table; a wrong column name or meaning is met in use and corrected in their own code. Its failure alone changes nothing for the buyer. Rated on the scale alone.

The claim concerns a field that is not in the release; if untrue, the engineers would at most see an extra placeholder column, which no stated threshold reaches and which does not affect evaluation or training. No way it could be untrue is material. Rated on the scale alone.

The claim describes the content of data that was excluded from the release; the team's engineers never meet it in use, and no way it could be untrue reaches a stated threshold or a part of the buyer's plan. Rated on the scale alone.

No stated threshold reaches a claim about which field carries provider information, and it falls under no item the buyer depends on. If it failed, the team's engineers would meet the failure while querying the released data and would act on it there. Rated on the scale alone.

A row count in the released database is reached by no stated threshold and no depended-on item. A discrepancy is something the team's engineers would meet and act on while working with the shipped database. Rated on the scale alone.

No stated threshold reaches the one-row-per-visit semantics or the per-patient encounter average, and no depended-on item names this part of the release. If it failed, the engineers would meet it while assembling patient timelines and act on it there. Rated on the scale alone.

The claim asserts the attending_name field is synthetic; if it failed by the names being real, the released data would not be fully synthetic, which under the buyer's terms ends the adoption and which no engineering effort by the team could cure. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "data that is not fully synthetic".

No stated threshold reaches this query recipe and no depended-on item names it. If joining and ordering did not reconstruct the timeline, the engineers would meet it while assembling multi-visit data and act on it there. Rated on the scale alone.

A table's row count is reached by no stated threshold and no depended-on item. Any discrepancy would be met by the engineers while inspecting the shipped database and acted on there. Rated on the scale alone.

No stated threshold or depended-on item reaches the existence or row count of this table. A discrepancy is something the team's engineers would meet and act on while using the data. Rated on the scale alone.

The nature of this field is reached by no stated threshold and no depended-on item. If the keys were not opaque integers into the annotation tables, the engineers would meet it while interpreting the field and act on it there. Rated on the scale alone.

No stated threshold reaches the row count or the section typing, and no depended-on item names this table. If the sections were not the retrieval passage unit, the engineers would meet that while running the retrieval task and act on it there. Rated on the scale alone.

The buyer's ground-truth threshold concerns ground truth or scoring not working as described, not a table's existence, row count or columns, and no other threshold or depended-on item reaches those. Any discrepancy would be met and acted on by the engineers while working with the database. Rated on the scale alone.

A table's row count and the 0–3 relevance scale are reached by no stated threshold and no depended-on item. A discrepancy would be met by the engineers while using the relevance data and acted on there. Rated on the scale alone.

No stated threshold reaches this table's row count or its keying to ground truth, and no depended-on item names it. Any discrepancy would be met and acted on while running the imaging-indication task. Rated on the scale alone.

Row counts of the knowledge-graph tables are reached by no stated threshold and no depended-on item. Discrepancies would be met by the engineers while inspecting or querying the graph and acted on there. Rated on the scale alone.

No stated threshold reaches the ontology coding of the graph — it is not ground truth, scoring, simulator faithfulness, split integrity or provenance — and no depended-on item names it. If the coding differed as described, the engineers would meet it while using the graph and act on it there. Rated on the scale alone.

The row counts and contents of the annotation tables are reached by no stated threshold and no depended-on item. Any discrepancy would be met and acted on by the engineers while working with the annotation data. Rated on the scale alone.

No stated threshold reaches the presence or absence of question text in the annotation tables: it is neither a leakage channel between splits nor a licence, scoring, simulator or validation matter. A person working with the annotation tables would act on the boundary and meet any difference in use, but on its own it changes nothing for the buyer's plan. Rated on the scale alone.

No stated threshold reaches the existence or contents of a release_info table. A person setting up the benchmark would read the version and change notes and would notice a missing table, but its absence changes how the release is inspected, not whether the plan holds. Rated on the scale alone.

The instance counts fall under the dataset's content and scale, an item the buyer uses rather than depends on, and no stated threshold reaches them. A count error is something the team's engineers can check directly against the shipped database and work around. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim could be untrue by the split labels being assigned at encounter level, so that one patient's encounters land in both the training pool and the held-out set. That is exactly the leakage the buyer named, and it would invalidate published results and reinforcement-learning training with no repair the team can make. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "leakage between the public, held-out and training splits".

The public split's size and its role as the reported benchmark fall under the dataset content and scale item the buyer uses, and no stated threshold reaches them. An error is checkable against the shipped database and the team runs its own evaluation regardless of which split the project reported. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The held-out split's size and the instruction not to train on it fall under the dataset content and scale item the buyer uses; no stated threshold reaches them, and the buyer's plan already trains only on the train split. A discrepancy is checkable by the team's engineers in the shipped data. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

Beyond the counts, the claim asserts the train split is usable for reinforcement learning with graph-derived rewards; if it is not, half the buyer's stated purpose, training the agent on the benchmark, fails, and the team would have to build its own reward service and episode harness rather than repair the split. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

No way the sampling description could be untrue, a different pool, strata or seed, is material: the actual split membership ships in the database and the membership script and can be inspected, so the description's accuracy changes documentation, not whether the plan holds, and a wrong seed does not un-reproduce a split whose members are recorded. Rated on the scale alone.

This is a claim about a document, and the script is not itself a fact the buyer relies on, such as a licence or ownership text, so it has no route to the buyer. A person determining which patients belong to the reinforcement-learning split would consult the script and meet its absence in use, which is not material on its own. Rated on the scale alone.

The distinctness of source questions concerns how the released data was built, an item the buyer uses rather than depends on, and no stated threshold reaches it; if encounters shared source questions the team's engineers can detect that in the shipped data, and evaluation on the actual encounters is unaffected. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim could be untrue by some patients sharing source material; where such patients fall in different splits, training would expose the source questions that held-out encounters derive from, contaminating the held-out set in a way the team cannot detect or repair without the project's records. That is a leakage channel of the kind the buyer named. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "leakage between the public, held-out and training splits".

The claim could be untrue by the database actually containing some raw source cards, board-question vignettes and answers, fact cards or source EHR sections; that would be source content shipped in the release whose distribution rights are unverified, the licence problem the buyer said ends the adoption and which no engineering effort cures. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a licence or data-provenance problem, such as source content the project may not distribute".

No stated threshold reaches the exclusion of model outputs and LLM call logs; they are neither patient data raising the synthetic-data threshold nor source content raising the licence threshold. A person using the database would act on knowing what it contains and meet any difference in use, which is not material on its own. Rated on the scale alone.

The claim could be untrue by the licensed SNOMED CT / LOINC terminology tables actually being shipped with the database; distributing licensed terminology without holding the licence is a licence problem the buyer said ends the adoption, and the team cannot cure it by removing the tables after relying on the release. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a licence or data-provenance problem".

The loader function falls under terminology handling, an item the buyer uses rather than depends on; if the function were missing or did not work, the team's engineers can obtain the terminology files and load them themselves at modest cost. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The relevance judgments are the ground truth for the evidence-retrieval task; if the chart-section judgments are absent or not as described, that ground truth does not work as described and the team would have to narrow what it publishes. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "ground truth or scoring that does not work as described".

The retired single-encounter task is not one of the four tasks the buyer's plan depends on, and no way the claim could be untrue changes the price, the terms or the plan; an engineer configuring evaluation would act on which tasks are present and meet any discrepancy there. Rated on the scale alone.

The split label names are acted on by anyone selecting data for evaluation or training, but a mismatch is a name difference noticed on first inspection and corrected without changing code, so it changes how the software is set up rather than whether the plan holds. Rated on the scale alone.

If the disclosed cleaning was not carried out, the shipped charts would carry the self-contradictory medication and history statements, duplicate problem-list entries and fragments the DATA_CARD says were removed, making the clinical content materially worse than described; the team cannot repair the data itself, and its published results would not support the claims it wants to make. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

If the release was not built by the pipeline as described — in particular if the profiles and notes were not derived from clustered question vignettes — the clinical content is not what the DATA_CARD says was derived from the education material, and the team could not stand behind the data's provenance in what it publishes; it cannot repair the data itself. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The presence or absence of the provenance pointers matters to an engineer parsing or auditing the profile files, and no way the claim could be untrue defeats an item the buyer depends on: the pointers are identifiers, not shipped content, and the team does not rebuild the data. Rated on the scale alone.

If the released data is not fully synthetic, the buyer's stated walk-away condition is met and no repair by the team cures it. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "data that is not fully synthetic".

If the generated content reproduces protectable source material, the release carries a copyright problem of the kind the buyer says ends adoption, and the team cannot cure it after the fact. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a licence or data-provenance problem".

If untrue because the profiles ship SNOMED CT or LOINC codes the project is not entitled to redistribute, the release would carry a licence problem of the kind the buyer says ends adoption, and shipped ICD codes in patient profiles would put the diagnosis reference where the agent can reach it. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a licence or data-provenance problem".

If the tables do not carry the codes as described, the diagnosis reference and scoring are broken; if the licensing characterizations are wrong — SNOMED CT content beyond identifiers and display names, or LOINC not redistributable — the release carries a licence problem the team cannot repair. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a licence or data-provenance problem".

If the stated licensing condition is wrong in the adverse direction — restrictions broader than disclosed — the team's use of the knowledge-graph's SNOMED CT content would face a licence problem it cannot repair after adoption. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a licence or data-provenance problem".

If the problem-list tool, the active_problems field or the FHIR Condition resource is absent or does not return the graph-derived reference, the ground truth and scoring do not work as described and the team's evaluation results and training rewards are meaningless. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "ground truth or scoring that does not work as described".

If the /env endpoints do not substitute the chart's documented history for the ground-truth diagnoses, the correct diagnoses reach the agent during episodes, contaminating evaluation results and reinforcement-learning rewards; the team would have to filter or fork the simulator's serving layer, which does not preserve the plan. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

If the assessment and plan sections are not hidden, the chart's diagnostic conclusions reach the agent during episodes, contaminating evaluation results and reinforcement-learning rewards; the team would have to filter or fork the simulator's serving layer, which does not preserve the plan. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim discloses a limit on evaluations that call the raw tool API, a path the team's plan does not use: it drives the environment and scoring through the /env endpoints and the provided client, which remain protected if the claim holds. If the disclosed boundary were different, engineers choosing a call path would meet it in use, and it would change how they run evaluations, not whether the plan holds. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim sits under the permitted-use boundary, which the buyer's plan does not touch: the team uses the data only to evaluate and train its agent, not for clinical care. No stated threshold reaches it, and no way it could be untrue would change the price, the terms or the plan. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim sits under the permitted-use boundary, which the buyer's plan does not touch: the team does not use the data for clinical decision-making and does not treat it as real patient data. No stated threshold reaches it, so no way it could be untrue is material. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim could be untrue because the clinical content derives from real patient records rather than medical education material; that is data that is not fully synthetic, and under the buyer's stated threshold adoption would end, since no repair by the team cures non-synthetic data. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "data that is not fully synthetic".

The claim is a hedged disclosure: as worded it fails only if the content is cleaner than described, which leaves the buyer's plan intact, and it sets no bound that worse artifacts could break. No stated threshold reaches it and no way it could be untrue is material. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

This is a documented command the team's engineers would run when loading the benchmark database into the simulator; if it were wrong they would meet the failure during setup and correct it — another module or path — without changing code, so no way it could be untrue is material. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

This is a documented command the team's engineers would run to load their own SNOMED CT / LOINC tables; if it were wrong they would meet the failure during setup and load the tables themselves, which the plan treats as cheap, so no way it could be untrue is material. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim describes how the released data was built; the team adopts the data as shipped and does not rerun the generation pipeline, so its engineers would not meet a failure of these stages in use. No stated threshold reaches it and no way it could be untrue changes the plan. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim could be untrue because the problem-list tool, the active_problems field or the FHIR Condition resource does not return the graph-derived ground-truth diagnoses with ICD-10 codes; the scoring reference for the diagnosis task would then be missing or wrong, defeating the buyer's evaluation and its reinforcement-learning rewards. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "ground truth or scoring that does not work as described".

The claim could be untrue because the /env endpoints or Harbor tasks serve the ground-truth diagnoses instead of the chart's documented history; the agent under test would then read the labels, contaminating rewards and inflating the results the team publishes, and no repair restores contaminated runs. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "ground truth or scoring that does not work as described".

The claim could be untrue because the assessment and plan sections are shown during episodes; the agent could then read the admitting assessment, which carries the diagnosis, contaminating rewards and inflating results, and the team's only remedy — filtering or forking the serving layer — is buyer-side engineering and does not hold the plan. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim asserts the pipeline's output records are synthetic; if they are not — if the benchmark database contains real patient data — the buyer's adoption ends and no local repair cures it. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "data that is not fully synthetic".

If the simulation platform is not faithful to Epic's interface in FHIR R4, OAuth2 or RBAC as claimed, evaluation and training against it would not transfer to the Epic-like deployment setting the buyer cares about, and the simulator is the project's core offering. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a simulator that is not FHIR R4 / OAuth2 / RBAC faithful as claimed".

If the benchmark cannot serve as a verifiable-reward environment, reinforcement learning on the training split — half the buyer's stated purpose — fails, and the buyer would have to build its own reward service and episode harness at significant cost. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

No stated threshold reaches the existence, authorship or title of a preprint, and the buyer's comparability with the published paper is an item it only uses, reporting under its own documented protocol if the preprint disappoints. Rated on the scale alone.

If the source content is in fact distributed with the project, the release ships material it may not be entitled to distribute — the provenance problem the buyer said would end the adoption, which the buyer cannot repair and could only cure by removing the affected material or walking away. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "source content the project may not distribute".

The ETL pipeline is an item the buyer does not use — it adopts the release as shipped and does not rebuild the database — and no stated threshold reaches the stage sequence or its naming. Rated on the scale alone.

The output database's format and location are details the buyer's engineers act on when loading the released benchmark, and a wrong path or format would surface during setup without changing whether the buyer's plan holds. No stated threshold reaches it and no way it could be untrue defeats an item the buyer depends on. Rated on the scale alone.

If epic_sim does not support FHIR R4, OAuth2 and RBAC as claimed, the buyer's evaluation and training would not transfer to the Epic-like setting it is adopting the simulator for, and replacing the simulator would be costly. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a simulator that is not FHIR R4 / OAuth2 / RBAC faithful as claimed".

If eval/ provides no working scoring, the ground truth and scoring the buyer is adopting do not work as described and its evaluation results and training rewards would be meaningless — the core of what it is adopting, which repair would make costly. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "ground truth or scoring that does not work as described".

The claim asserts the patients are synthetic; if the released profiles are not fully synthetic — if real patient data is included — the buyer's adoption ends under its own stated threshold and no patch could cure it. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "data that is not fully synthetic".

A note count is a documented figure the buyer's engineers would check when inspecting the shipped data files, and a wrong count on its own changes nothing about the buyer's plan. No stated threshold reaches it and no way it could be untrue defeats an item the buyer depends on. Rated on the scale alone.

If the splits are not partitioned at the patient level, a patient appears in more than one split — the leakage the buyer said would change the terms, invalidating its published results and any reinforcement-learning training. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "leakage between the public, held-out and training splits".

The held-out split's size is a documented figure the buyer's engineers would act on when running evaluation and would meet any discrepancy in use; a wrong count reaches no stated threshold and on its own leaves a usable evaluation path. Rated on the scale alone.

If the training split is materially smaller than the 800 patients claimed, it is not usable for the reinforcement-learning training that is half the buyer's stated purpose, and the buyer cannot repair a thin split itself without the project's sampling records. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The ETL pipeline is an item the buyer does not use — it adopts the release as shipped and does not rebuild the database — and no stated threshold reaches the pipeline's existence or location. Rated on the scale alone.

The ETL pipeline is an item the buyer does_not_use, and no stated threshold reaches a claim about the etl/ directory's contents, so no way it could be untrue reaches the buyer's plan. Rated on the scale alone.

The migrations and tests are operational details a person setting up or running the simulator would encounter and could correct during setup; their absence would not defeat any item the buyer depends on. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The claim asserts several things, and it could be untrue in ways that defeat items the buyer depends on: if the task definitions are absent or empty the four benchmark tasks cannot run, and if the CLI is absent the eval.cli commands named in the reproducible-evaluation item do not exist, so published evaluation could not be stood behind without significant work. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

No stated threshold reaches a claim about the inclusion of ICD-10 validation — the scoring threshold concerns ground truth and scoring working as described, not the presence of a validation feature — and no depends item names it. A person running evaluation would act on the feature and meet its absence in use, without the plan failing. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The auditing and analysis scripts fall under the methodology-artifacts item the buyer uses, not depends on; their absence would cost the team a means of checking how the data was built but would not defeat the plan. A person operating the release would act on the scripts and meet their absence in use. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The compose-stack part falls under an item the buyer uses, and the all-in-one-image part falls under the alternative-packaging item the buyer does_not_use. A person setting up the stack would act on the build files and meet any failure at first run, and could correct it without changing the plan. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.
Harbor task templates and the Apptainer definition fall under the alternative-packaging item the buyer does_not_use, and no stated threshold reaches them. Rated on the scale alone.

The shipped data files fall under items the buyer uses (dataset content and distribution mechanics); the synthetic-data and licence thresholds concern the data's nature, not which files ship, and a missing file would be met during setup. A person setting up the stack would act on the files and meet their absence at first boot. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The compose stack is an item the buyer uses; a person setting it up would act on the build and meet any failure at first run, and the simulator could be served directly without changing the plan. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The service versions are setup details under the compose-stack item the buyer uses; a person running the stack would meet any failure at first boot and could correct the configuration without changing the plan. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

First-boot loading is part of the compose-stack item the buyer uses; a failure would be met and corrected during setup and does not by itself reach a threshold or a depends item. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

Serving the simulator through compose falls under the compose-stack item the buyer uses, and the simulator-fidelity threshold concerns how faithfully it simulates, not whether the stack serves it; a failure would be met at setup and the simulator could be served directly without changing the plan. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

A load-time figure is not something a person setting up or operating the stack would act on, and no threshold or depends item reaches it; a slower load would change expectations during setup, not whether the plan holds. Rated on the scale alone.

The documentation URL is a location detail a person operating the stack would act on and would meet any failure immediately; its failure changes how the stack is accessed, not whether the plan holds. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The log line is a readiness signal a person operating the stack would act on, and the 1,268-patient figure sits under a dataset-scale item the buyer uses; a missing line or a differing count would be met in setup and does not by itself reach a threshold or a depends item. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

If evaluation or tests do not run inside the image against the loaded database, the team's engineers meet this on first use and correct their compose or entrypoint setup themselves; no stated threshold reaches the container boundary and no depends item turns on it. Rated on the scale alone.

If the documented `eval.cli run` command does not exist or does not accept the task, split and strategy options shown, the documented evaluation path fails, the buyer's reproducible-runs item is defeated, and published results cannot be produced as described; re-establishing reproducibility unaided is, per the reliance statement, significant work for the team. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

A missing or unrunnable test suite would be met by the team's own engineers while setting up and worked around without affecting the plan; no stated threshold reaches it and no depends item covers the tests. Rated on the scale alone.

Results landing somewhere other than ./results would be noticed immediately in use and corrected by fixing the host mount, a setup change rather than a change to whether the plan holds. Rated on the scale alone.

Port overrides are a setup convenience; if the variables do not work the engineers would notice while starting the stack and adapt, with no effect on validity, reproducibility or any depends item. Rated on the scale alone.

Idempotence of the startup load affects restart convenience only; its failure would be met in operation and worked around without changing code or defeating any depends item. Rated on the scale alone.

A forced-reload flag is an operational convenience; if it does not work the engineers would notice and reload the database by another means, which does not change whether the plan holds. Rated on the scale alone.

Where the terminology endpoints read from is an implementation detail behind the documented interface; the disclosed emptiness of the table (claim 48) means any failure shows up in use and is a data-loading matter, not a failure of FHIR R4, OAuth2 or RBAC faithfulness. Rated on the scale alone.

If the release could in fact pre-fill the table the claim's failure only eases setup, and otherwise the team's engineers load the terminology themselves; a person setting the software up would act on the claim and meet its failure there. Rated on the scale alone.

Licensing requirements for SNOMED CT and LOINC fall under terminology handling the practice rates as cheaply repairable — the engineers obtain the files and hold the licences themselves — and no way the claim could be untrue defeats a depends item or a stated threshold; it concerns third-party terminology the release does not ship, not the project's distribution rights. Rated on the scale alone.

If parts of the benchmark in fact require SNOMED CT or LOINC, the engineers would meet this while setting up and load the missing terminology without changing code, so the plan as stated still holds. Rated on the scale alone.

If ICD-10-CM is not public domain, the benchmark's automatically loaded core terminology carries licence restrictions the team's adoption and published results would inherit, and a licence defect is not something the team can repair — the adoption would end under the buyer's own trigger. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a licence or data-provenance problem, such as source content the project may not distribute or data that is not fully synthetic".

A failed automatic download would be met on first boot and corrected by loading the CMS files by hand, a path the release itself documents; no threshold or depends item turns on the download happening automatically. Rated on the scale alone.
A disable flag that does not work is a setup detail the engineers would notice and work around in operation, with no effect on the plan. Rated on the scale alone.

The offline load path is one of two ways to obtain ICD-10-CM; if it fails, the automatic download or a manual load remains, and nothing in a stated threshold or depends item turns on this route. Rated on the scale alone.

Loading SNOMED CT and LOINC is a setup step the team's engineers would perform, and a failure in the mount-and-restart instructions would surface there; it changes how the stack is set up, not whether the plan holds. No stated threshold reaches terminology loading, and the reliance item for it is a 'uses' item. Rated on the scale alone.

The filename patterns are what a setting-up engineer would rely on to place the files; a pattern that does not match would be met and corrected during setup. It affects configuration, not the validity of the benchmark or simulator. Rated on the scale alone.

A release version or layout that does not work would be discovered by the engineer performing the load and worked around by obtaining a different version or flattening files. It is a setup detail with no route to the buyer's thresholds. Rated on the scale alone.

Idempotence of the terminology loader is an operational behaviour an engineer rerunning the stack would act on and meet any failure of directly. Its failure would not reach the buyer's plan for the benchmark or simulator. Rated on the scale alone.

'Nothing else needs to change' is a setup instruction; if further configuration were needed, the engineer would meet it while mounting the directory and restarting. It changes the setup effort, not whether the adoption's purpose holds. Rated on the scale alone.

A skip condition on the terminology tests is a detail a developer running the test suite after loading would act on and notice if wrong. It concerns test behaviour, not benchmark validity, scoring, or simulator fidelity. Rated on the scale alone.
